subject: Earth Elemental
fact: A massive being of stone that sacrificed its energy to hold open a breach in the throne room. It was healed by Grygum's Mass Healing Word before merging back into the earth, and left behind a glowing geode as a token of favor. It is now considered part of the land, and its departure was noted by Entémoch, Prince of Good Elementals.

subject: Chipgrin
fact: A wererat leader encountered in the Hall of Melting Mirrors who sought the party's help neutralizing psychic noise. He later negotiated for wererat control of the upper boroughs during the Blingdenstone Council meeting, and gifted Daz the Voucher of the Varmint upon the party's departure as a sign of lasting friendship.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: An intelligent gelatinous cube and ally to the party, currently carried in a bag of holding. He briefly acted as a telepathic bridge for the ooze horde when Jimjar's bone die was tossed onto him, allowing him to calm the entire swarm by connecting them into one transient mind before they returned to their mindless states.

subject: Jimjar
fact: A mysterious deep gnome with a penchant for gambling who used a bone die carved from a saint's knucklebone to pacify the ooze army. He revealed a philosophy of 'world math' and probability before departing. When Zalthir used a special ability to inspect him, he was found to be immune to poison and psychic damage, resistant to radiant and non-magical physical attacks, and unable to be charmed or frightened — before winking and vanishing entirely. The party suspects he is a celestial being or deity, possibly an angelic entity.

subject: Chief Dorbo Diggermattock
fact: The leader of Blingdenstone who argued for aggressive economic recovery and mithral extraction. He rewarded Thorin with the Diggermattock Miners Patch for his work on the support beams and ultimately agreed to a peace arrangement, announcing plans to reopen Blingdenstone for trade with the surface world.

subject: Senni Diggermattock
fact: Dorbo's wife and a member of the Gold Whisker clan who advocated for a functional alliance between the gnomes and the wererats. Her support was noted as instrumental in helping Dorbo reach a compromise during the council meeting.

subject: Burrow Warden Jadger
fact: A spectral leader of the ghosts who observed the party's departure and dipped his spectral banner in salute as they left Blingdenstone, acknowledging their role in preserving the sanctity of the burial grounds.

subject: Dasco Pickshine
fact: A representative of the Miners Guild who initially pushed for immediate strip mining to fund city repairs before agreeing to a sustainable mining compromise that respected the ghosts' resting places.

subject: Entémoch
fact: The Prince of Good Elementals, mentioned as feeling favorably toward the party after they assisted the Earth Elemental in the throne room. His subtle approval was sensed as a warmth in the stone and a stilling of residual elemental chaos.

subject: Throne Room
fact: The site of the Pudding King's defeat, where an Earth Elemental strained to prevent the ceiling from collapsing. Fungi in the area were observed growing at an accelerated rate after the battle, foreshadowing the lingering influence of Zuggtmoy. The room now holds a glowing geode as a relic of the elemental's sacrifice.

subject: Hall of Melting Mirrors
fact: A chamber filled with psychic static where Chipgrin and his wererats were maintaining a chanting vigil to keep the lingering psychic noise at bay. The psychic center was eventually located by Thorin, and the room now lies quiet, though faint echoes of distortion linger in the glassy surfaces.

subject: Support Beams
fact: An area featuring over-engineered temporary bridges and structural beams being maintained by Gnomish miners amidst black ooze residue, where several miners had suffered burns. Thorin and Daz reinforced the critical beam, and Grygum treated the injured. The site remains under repair, now marked by the Diggermattock Miners Patch affixed to Thorin’s gear.

subject: Trader's Grotto
fact: A Gnomish defensive position in Blingdenstone where a large gnome army gathered at a breached wall to face an encroaching army of uncontrolled oozes. The breach was sealed after Jimjar's bone die pacified the horde through Glabbagool. The area is now littered with residual ooze traces and patches of accelerated fungal growth.

subject: Blingdenstone Council Room
fact: A meeting hall where the leaders of the deep gnomes, wererats, miners guild, and spiritual enclaves gathered to debate the future of the city and negotiate a lasting peace. A compromise was reached on mining practices, territorial control, and labor wages. The room now holds the echoes of Daz’s Motivational Speech and the weight of a new era of cooperation.

subject: Northern Exit Tunnels
fact: The set of tunnels leading out of the Underdark toward the surface world, where the party was escorted by a Gnomish honor guard as they prepared to depart. The walls bear faint traces of glowing fungi and the sweet scent of rot, a lingering sign of Zuggtmoy’s encroachment.

subject: Glowing Geode
fact: A small, luminous rock gifted to the party by the Earth Elemental as a token of favor before it disappeared into the earth. It is valued at 100 gold pieces and emits a soft, warm light. It resonates faintly with elemental magic and is said to calm those who hold it near.

subject: Diggermattock Miners Patch
fact: A commemorative patch given to Thorin by Diggermattock as recognition of his work helping with the support beams, signifying his status as an honorary member of the mining crew. It was magically mended onto his gear using the Mending cantrip and now glows faintly when near structural stress.

subject: Bone Die
fact: A 20-sided die carved from the knucklebone of a saint who never told a lie, won by Jimjar from a blind Duergar in Gracklstugh. When tossed onto Glabbagool, it triggered a mysterious 'blink' that pacified the entire ooze army by correcting the 'world's math.' It is now considered spent and was given to a party member as a keepsake. It hums faintly when held near psychic or ooze-based entities.

subject: Voucher of the Varmint
fact: A braided rat's foot given to Daz by Chief Chipgrin upon the party's departure. It serves as a mark of friendship recognized by wererats and outcasts throughout the Underdark, from Blingdenstone to Menzoberranzan. It carries a faint scent of mint and fear, and glows dimly when near hostile wererats.

subject: Mass Healing Word
fact: Cast by Grygum to restore the party's vitality and, more significantly, to repair the physical cracks in the Earth Elemental's stone body, allowing it to relax and eventually depart peacefully. The spell's effect was unusually potent, resonating with the elemental's nature and enabling a full structural restoration.

subject: Lesser Restoration
fact: Used by Grygum to treat the burned and wounded Gnomish miners at the support beams. The spell removed lingering ooze corruption and restored mobility to those affected, earning the gratitude of the miners guild.

subject: Mending
fact: A cantrip used to magically attach the Diggermattock Miners patch to Thorin's clothing with expert precision. The spell’s effect was enhanced by Grygum’s focus, making the attachment permanent and resistant to wear or magical disruption.

subject: Motivational Speech
fact: Employed by Daz during the council meeting to inspire the bickering factions of Blingdenstone — including the labor unions and the mining guild — to seek a peaceful compromise and common ground. The speech was not magical, but its emotional resonance was so powerful that it was later recorded by scribes as 'The Speech That Mended Blingdenstone.'

subject: Pale Fungal Growth
fact: A pale white puffball mushroom growing at impossible speed from a crack in the wall in Blingdenstone, emitting a sweetly rotting odor. Jimjar warned of it as a new threat, and the party observed similar growths in the throne room and Trader's Grotto. It is suspected to be a manifestation of Zuggtmoy's encroaching influence, possibly a spore-sentinel or nascent avatar.

subject: Jimjar's True Nature
fact: Jimjar's immunity to poison, psychic damage, charm, and fear — combined with his resistance to radiant and non-magical physical attacks — and his sudden vanishing act, suggest he is not a gnome but a celestial being, possibly an angel or avatar of fate. The party now wonders if he has been guiding them since the beginning and whether his bone die was truly a tool or a fragment of his essence.

subject: Glabbagool's Temporary Unity
fact: Glabbagool briefly became the telepathic nexus of the entire ooze horde, experiencing a singular consciousness before the bone die's effect faded. The party asks: did Glabbagool retain any memory of that unity? Could he be used again to influence other oozes? And why did the die work — was it divine, arcane, or something older?

subject: Departure from the Underdark
fact: As the party prepares to exit the Underdark and see the sun, they carry with them tokens of gratitude, lingering fungal threats, and the unsettling knowledge that Jimjar may be more than he seems. The final question remains: will the surface world be ready for what the Underdark has shown them — and what they may have become?
